neet_phy_u04_t01_1.working: K = p²/2m. Doubling p (a 100% increase) makes K four times larger, so K increases by 300%.

neet_phy_u04_t01_2.working: dU/dx = x² - 4 = 0 gives x = ±2. d²U/dx² = 2x is positive at x = +2, so U is a minimum there and the equilibrium is stable.

neet_phy_u04_t01_3.working: K = p²/2m with equal p, so K is proportional to 1/m. K1:K2 = 4:1.

neet_phy_u04_t01_4.working: Minimum of U is stable (III). Maximum of U is unstable (IV). Constant U is neutral (I). dU/dx > 0 means F = -dU/dx < 0, so the force is along -x (II).

neet_phy_u04_t01_5.working: A is true: KE = mv²/2 cannot be negative. B is true: PE depends on the reference level. C is false: friction is non-conservative, so no PE exists for it. D is false: for equal p, the heavier body has less KE. E is true: tripling v gives 9 times the KE. Correct set is A, B, E.
